subject: Hosted evaluation: deployment preference & rate-limit clarification
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@mediavatech.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@mediavatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted evaluation: deployment preference & rate-limit clarification

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum:

1) Deployment preference: You mentioned wanting a low-friction path for an initial proof-of-concept and then deciding between Dedicated or Private later. For most customers on a similar cadence we recommend starting on Hosted API to validate product/UX and request patterns, then migrate to Dedicated when you need predictable throughput or strict data residency.

2) Quickstart: I attached a short Hosted Quickstart guide (PDF) that outlines the minimal steps to get the integration up and running (API keys, rate-limit headers, sample curl + SDK).

3) Endpoints & rate limits: The quickstart includes our standard Hosted endpoints and token accounting, but two specifics we flagged on the call: burst behavior (short spikes) and sustained QPS targets. To avoid surprises we can provision a temporary elevated rate cap during the pilot window.

4) Metrics & observability: For the evaluation we'll enable per-route latency/cost dashboards and a short tracing hook so you can measure end-to-end latency from your app.

Next steps I propose:
- Connor: provision a temporary hosted rate increase for the pilot (2x standard) and share an activation token by Monday.
- Marissa: send the mini quickstart and a suggested simple traffic profile you can run (100 concurrent users, ~8k tokens/day) so we can size caching/batching.
- Alicia/Tom: confirm pilot start date and any compliance items that would push you toward Dedicated or Private immediately (e.g., PII restrictions, audit process).

If that looks good I'll draft a short mutual action plan and share a MA/terms doc we can redline.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0139

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@mediavatech.com>

Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@mediavatech.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: deployment preference & rate-limit clarification

Thanks Connor — really helpful demo. Quick answers from our side:

- Preference: We prefer starting Hosted for speed of iteration. Our legal team will only push to Dedicated/Private if our ingestion of customer PII actually requires different residency controls; for now the pilot will use obfuscated test data.
- Pilot timeline: target start 2026-01-26, 3-week window.
- Traffic profile: expecting short bursts during business hours (9–11am PT) with peak QPS ~60 and average QPS ~12; payloads are typically 150–300 tokens per request.

Questions we still have:
1) Will the temporary elevated cap you mentioned cover sustained peaks at 60 QPS for a few hours, or is that intended only for short bursts?
2) Do rate-limit headers include per-minute and per-second limits? We need to implement exponential backoff/reslices on our side.
3) Are there recommended endpoints for multi-region failover or do we need to route from our side?

We appreciate the quickstart doc — please send the token and any sample load scripts.

Best,
Alicia
Director of Product Integrations
MediaVaTech

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@mediavatech.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@mediavatech.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Hosted evaluation: deployment preference & rate-limit clarification

Hi all — following up with technical details so Alicia and Tom can finalize integration work.

1) Elevated cap: We can provision a temporary hosted rate increase that supports sustained 60 QPS for a 3-week pilot window. This is done by creating a scoped API key tied to the pilot account and an override on the Hosted tier for the pilot dates. Note: sustained high QPS will increase per-token billing but we can track and cap monthly spend per the MA.

2) Rate-limit headers: Hosted returns X-RateLimit-Limit (per minute), X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset (epoch seconds). For burst protection we also return X-Phase-Burst (short window) when continuous bursts are detected; we recommend implementing both per-second client-side smoothing and exponential backoff with jitter. Sample pseudo-code in the quickstart shows the header parsing and retry strategy.

3) Multi-region endpoints: For now, Hosted has regional endpoints (us-west, us-east, eu-central). We recommend routing from your side to the nearest region; Redwood can also configure a managed failover route if you prefer. For the pilot we suggest using us-west to minimize latency.

4) Attachments: Attached is the quickstart PDF and an initial MA draft. The quickstart includes cURL/SDK examples, the sample load script, and a tiny Node.js example that implements backoff using the rate-limit headers.

If you want, Aditya and I can run a short onboarding call the first day of the pilot to watch a few requests and verify headers/metrics.

Thanks —
Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments (2): redwood_quickstart_hosted.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB), ma_draft_mediavatech_v1.docx (DOCX, 45KB)
